resources.string: Starting dimensions for two active elements with gamma matching, scaled from a published ANSYS HFSS model.
Enter a frequency from 100 to 1500 MHz.

Changing the frequency scales all model dimensions, including diameters D and d and gap h. For example, D drops from 12.6 to 4.2 mm when going from 145 to 435 MHz. Check the match of the resulting build if you change a diameter, the gap or the material.
Measure MR and MF along each element from the boom centerline to the gamma connection. A is the spacing between the element axes. The inset shows the gap h between conductor surfaces.
HB9CV diagram showing both active elements, gamma arms, feed point and conductor cross section.
MR and MF are mounting dimensions. The full blank depends on the bends and feed fittings.
Enter both end overhangs to calculate the boom length and mark the element positions.
LR position from the rear end
LF position from the rear end
With f in MHz, wavelength λ = 299.792458 / f in metres. Multiply each 144 MHz dimension below by 144 / f. Estimated capacitance C = 2304 / f in pF. Boom length = A + both end overhangs.
To improve front-to-back suppression, lengthen LR and shorten LF by the same amount. Fine-tune A and check the radiation pattern.
For minimum SWR, move both gamma taps by the same amount and adjust the series capacitor while measuring the assembled antenna.
The original publication includes simulated impedance, SWR, gain, front-to-back ratio, radiation pattern and S11 plots.
